source_text:
Προσευξαμένου μου ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ καὶ καθίσαντος εἰς τὴν κλίνην εἰσῆλθεν ἀνήρ τις ἔνδοξος τῇ ὄψει, σχήματι ποιμενικῷ, περικείμενος δέρμα αἴγειον λευκὸν καὶ πήραν ἔχων ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων καὶ ῥάβδον εἰς τὴν χεῖρα. καὶ ἠσπάσατό με, κἀγὼ ἀντησπασάμην αὐτόν.
καὶ εὐθὺς παρεκάθισέν μοι καὶ λέγει μοι: Ἀπεστάλην ὑπὸ τοῦ σεμνοτάτου ἀγγέλου, ἵνα μετὰ σοῦ οἰκήσω τὰς λοιπὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ζωῆς σου.
ἔδοξα ἐγώ, ὅτι πάρεστιν ἐκπειράζων με, καὶ λέγω αὐτῷ: Σὺ γὰρ τίς εἶ; ἐγὼ γάρ, φημί, γινώσκω, ᾧ παρεδόθην. λέγει μοι: Οὐκ ἐπιγινώσκεις με; Οὔ, φημί. Ἐγώ, φησίν, εἰμὶ ὁ ποιμήν, ᾧ παρεδόθης.
ἔτι λαλοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἠλλοιώθη ἡ ἰδέα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπέγνων αὐτόν, ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ἦν, ᾧ παρεδόθην, καὶ εὐθὺς συνεχύθην καὶ φόβος με ἔλαβεν καὶ ὅλος συνεκόπην ἀπὸ τῆς λύπης, ὅτι οὕτως αὐτῷ ἀπεκρίθην πονηρῶς καὶ ἀφρόνως.
ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθείς μοι λέγει: Μὴ συγχύννου, ἀλλὰ ἰσχυροποιοῦ ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς μου αἷς σοι μέλλω ἐντέλλεσθαι. ἀπεστάλην γάρ, φησίν, ἵνα ἃ εἶδες πρότερον πάντα σοι πάλιν δείξω, αὐτὰ τὰ κεφάλαια τὰ ὄντα ὑμῖν σύμφορα. πρῶτον πάντων τὰς ἐντολάς μου γράψον καὶ τὰς παραβολάς: τὰ δὲ ἕτερα, καθώς σοι δείξω, οὕτως γράψεις: διὰ τοῦτο, φησίν, ἐντέλλομαί σοι πρῶτον γράψαι τὰς ἐντολὰς καὶ παραβολάς, ἵνα ὑπὸ χεῖρα ἀναγινώσκῃς αὐτὰς καὶ δυνηθῇς φυλάξαι αὐτάς.
ἔγραψα οὖν τὰς ἐντολὰς καὶ παραβολάς, καθὼς ἐνετείλατό μοι.
ἐὰν οὖν ἀκούσαντες αὐτὰς φυλάξητε καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς πορευθῆτε καὶ ἐργάσησθε αὐτὰς ἐν καθαρᾷ καρδίᾳ, ἀπολήμψεσθε ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, ὅσα ἐπηγγείλατο ὑμῖν: ἐὰν δὲ ἀκούσαντες μὴ μετανοήσητε, ἀλλ’ ἔτι προσθῆτε ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν, ἀπολήμψεσθε παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου τὰ ἐναντία. ταῦτά μοι πάντα οὕτως γράψαι ὁ ποιμὴν ἐνετείλατο, ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς μετανοίας.
thought_title: The Shepherd arrives and commands Hermas to write
orientation: Hermas is at home after prayer when a man dressed as a shepherd comes in. He is the angel of repentance, the Shepherd who gives the book its name, and he tells Hermas to write down the commandments and parables that follow.
pass_a_gloss: When I had prayed in the house and sat down on the bed, a certain man entered, glorious in appearance, in shepherd's clothing, wearing a white goatskin and having a pouch on his shoulders and a staff in his hand. And he greeted me, and I greeted him in return. And immediately he sat down beside me and says to me: I was sent by the most reverend angel, so that I might dwell with you the remaining days of your life. I thought that he was present testing me, and I say to him: Who are you? For I, I say, know the one to whom I was handed over. He says to me: Do you not recognize me? No, I say. I, he says, am the shepherd, to whom you were handed over. While he was still speaking, his appearance changed, and I recognized him, that he was the one to whom I was handed over, and immediately I was confounded and fear took hold of me and I was wholly crushed with grief, because I had answered him so wickedly and foolishly. But he answered me and says: Do not be confounded, but be strengthened in my commandments which I am about to command you. For I was sent, he says, so that all the things you saw before I might show you again, the very main points that are beneficial for you. First of all write my commandments and the parables; but the other things, just as I show you, so you will write. For this reason, he says, I command you first to write the commandments and parables, so that you may read them at hand and be able to keep them. So I wrote the commandments and parables, just as he commanded me. If therefore, having heard them, you keep them and walk in them and do them in a pure heart, you will receive from the Lord whatever he promised you; but if, having heard, you do not repent, but still add to your sins, you will receive from the Lord the opposite things. All these things the shepherd commanded me to write in this way, the angel of repentance.

choices.why: σχῆμα here denotes outward appearance or dress; 'clothing' conveys the visible form without implying a costume or disguise
rejected: in the guise of a shepherd

choices.why: δέρμα is a hide or skin; αἴγειον specifies goat; keeping 'goatskin' preserves the material specificity
σεμνός carries dignity and reverence; 'most reverend' preserves the superlative and the honorific tone
the middle/passive imperative has a reflexive force; 'be strengthened' keeps the command directed at Hermas's own resolve
the idiom means readily available for use; 'at hand' is the natural English equivalent
the neuter plural substantive refers to the opposite of the promised blessings; keeping the plural preserves the breadth of what is meant

pass_b_english: After I had prayed at home and sat down on my bed, a man came in, glorious to look at and dressed as a shepherd. He had a white goatskin wrapped around him, a bag on his shoulders, and a staff in his hand. He greeted me, and I greeted him in return.
At once he sat down beside me and said, “I have been sent by the most revered angel to live with you for the rest of the days of your life.”

I thought he had come to tempt me, and I said to him, “And who are you? For I know the one to whom I was handed over.” He said to me, “Do you not recognize me?” “No,” I said. “I am the Shepherd,” he said, “the one to whom you were handed over.”

While he was still speaking, his appearance changed, and I recognized him. He was the one to whom I had been handed over. At once I was thrown into confusion. Fear seized me, and I was utterly broken with grief, because I had answered him so wickedly and so foolishly.

But he answered me, “Do not be confused. Be strong in my commandments, which I am about to give you. For I was sent,” he said, “to show you again everything you saw before, the main points that are helpful for you all. First of all, write down my commandments and the parables. The rest you shall write just as I show you. This is why,” he said, “I command you to write the commandments and parables first: so that you may have them at hand to read and be able to keep them.”
So I wrote down the commandments and parables, just as he commanded me.

So then, if you hear them and keep them, if you walk in them and carry them out with a pure heart, you will receive from the Lord all that he promised you. But if you hear them and do not repent, but go on adding to your sins, you will receive the opposite from the Lord. All these things the Shepherd, the angel of repentance, commanded me to write just so.

checks.via: blind check of the tuned English, clean at round 0 (tune_check.py)

polish.changed: Clarified that the Shepherd speaks the final conditional warning, standardized 'the Shepherd' as the title for the angel of repentance, and kept 'the most reverend angel' as the distinct sender.

notes.quote: If, then, you hear them and keep them
notes.why: Unclear who speaks: Shepherd, Hermas, or editorial voice

notes.quote: the shepherd, the angel of repentance
notes.why: The same figure is called 'the shepherd,' 'the angel of repentance,' and 'the Shepherd' with inconsistent capitalization.
notes.fix: Standardize to 'the Shepherd (the angel of repentance)'.

notes.why: The same angel who hands Hermas over to the Shepherd is called by different titles.
notes.fix: Use one title consistently, e.g., 'the glorious angel'.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'angel of repentance' for ἄγγελος τῆς μετανοίας.
last_rejected.fix: the most reverend angel of repentance
last_rejected.ruling: σεμνοτάτου ἀγγέλου is a distinct phrase from ἄγγελος τῆς μετανοίας; no glossary conflict exists.

last_rejected.why: συγχύννου means 'troubled/disturbed', not 'confused'; repeated in next clause.
last_rejected.ruling: συγχύννου includes 'confused' within its semantic range; not a major meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: you hear them and keep them, walk in them, and practice them
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐὰν οὖν ἀκούσαντες αὐτὰς φυλάξητε καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς πορευθῆτε καὶ ἐργάσησθε αὐτὰς
last_rejected.why: The Greek is second person plural, but context shows the Shepherd is addressing Hermas who writes for the Church; English 'you' obscures this is a general address to readers.
last_rejected.fix: if, then, they hear them and keep them...
last_rejected.ruling: English 'you' can render Greek plural; no meaning lost. Mere preference, not a real error.
